name: Arah
overview: Arah is a male figure mentioned in the book of Nehemiah, specifically identified as the father of Shecaniah. There is no tribal affiliation or additional personal notes recorded about him in Scripture. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical in nature.
namesAndTitles: The name Arah means 'he wanders' in Hebrew. It is a proper name and not indicated as being given directly by God. This meaning may reflect a characteristic or family tradition but is not elaborated upon in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Arah as the father of Shecaniah, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships or connections are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Arah's significance lies in his genealogical role within the post-exilic community described in Nehemiah. By being the father of Shecaniah, he is part of the lineage that contributes to the restoration efforts of Israel after the exile. Though his personal story is not expanded, his mention helps preserve the continuity of God's people during a critical period of rebuilding.
